correctness.rationale: Variation of constants yields an exact solution for all finite u and nonnegative input-independent initial conditions. Dose-zero differentiation yields strictly positive P,Q and exact P-y0Q slope. The Gaussian comparison integral obeys a proved H(z)~1/z law, and small-window squeeze plus a bounded complement establishes C/logu->1/2. Negative initial slope and divergent high-input response force an interior global minimum by compactness. A stand-alone RK4 test reproduces the explicit sign and independent finite-dose behavior; it does not certify the limit.

Residual historical-priority risk remains, especially general feedforward asymptotics.

value.rationale: The published model’s central interpretation concerns monotone cumulative responses under adaptation. The exact output-preload threshold exposes a rigorously nonmonotone regime and a positive-input dose minimizing cumulative exposure. The universal half-log-dose scaling identifies the singular boundary-layer mechanism and guarantees eventual rebound regardless of initial states; these are physically interpretable mathematical boundaries beyond a single numerical counterexample.
